index_level_findings.finding: 9 of 9 Sprint 2 stories (DASH-STORY-012..020) have at least one candidate at or above the 0.75 threshold; no story required a force-assignment or a below-threshold fallback. DASH-STORY-020 has the most marginal above-threshold score in the sprint (python-backend-engineer, 0.7645) - see AR0-S2-F4.

python-backend-engineer is the top-scoring (and assigned) candidate on 8 of 9 Sprint 2 stories (013, 014, 015, 016, 017, 018, 019, 020) - 42 of 47 story points, 89% concentration - sharper than Sprint 1's already-flagged 64% (AR0-F2). Combined with Sprint 1, python-backend-engineer now holds 15 of 20 stories across both sprints (75%). This is a system-design bottleneck finding, not a routing defect: the HLD locks one Python 3.12 codebase, so concentration is the honest scoring result. The user reviewed a rebalance option (SP2-DEC-004, 2026-09-20) and deferred it rather than reassigning - database-engineer's above-threshold showings on DASH-STORY-015 (0.7600), DASH-STORY-017 (0.7645) and DASH-STORY-018 (0.7905) remain a pre-scored fallback roster if python-backend-engineer becomes the critical path during Phase B execution grouping.

The database-storage-engineer name-similarity trap was scored and explicitly rejected again on DASH-STORY-012 (0.2875, below threshold) - the identical rejection reasoning ar0_routing_index.json applied to it for DASH-STORY-002 in Sprint 1 (builds a database's own storage-engine internals, not application-layer schema on top of PostgreSQL). Recorded with its score so a later reviewer sees the rejection was measured, not assumed.

DASH-STORY-020 (DSHN-69) has a single valid implementer (python-backend-engineer, 0.7645 - the most marginal above-threshold score in Sprint 2) for a story whose decisive content is per-subject cryptographic key lifecycle management and India data-residency bucket provisioning. Neither cloud-security-architect (0.4600, right skills - data-security-privacy-core, india-cyber-regulatory-core - but no Edit tool) nor crypto-security-specialist (0.4100, right skills - cryptography-core, india-cyber-regulatory-core - but no Edit tool, explicitly audit-only) clears threshold as an IMPLEMENTER. Neither would be a compliant force-assignment (both below 0.75 AND structurally lack an Edit tool). The user accepted this implementer risk and authorized both non-blocking advisory reviews (SP2-DEC-001 on 2026-09-19, SP2-DEC-002 on 2026-09-20); OAQ-10's legal question (whether crypto-shredding satisfies DPDP Act 2023 erasure) stays explicitly open regardless of either review's outcome. Tracked as routing gap AR1-S2-G1 in the upstream assignment file.

The P1 security override (Maker-Checker gate, reviewer distinct from implementer) fired for exactly one Sprint 2 story: DASH-STORY-018, on the literal cross-tenant-isolation criterion (AC-008-3 / HLD threat I-5) - a direct, non-analogical match, confirmed mandatory and not waived by user decision SP2-DEC-005 (2026-09-20). DASH-STORY-020 was considered against the same three literal P1 criteria and did NOT trigger (it touches Zone 8, not Zone 7; it implements adapter-internal behavior behind the existing frozen ZoneRepository port rather than modifying the port interface; and in-region bucket provisioning is data-residency, not cross-tenant isolation) - it was routed to a non-blocking advisory review instead of an invented P1 extension, the same discipline ar1_assignments.json applied to DASH-STORY-003's DPDP obligation in Sprint 1 (AR1-G3).

Two of the sprint's three narrowest margins involve database-engineer as a genuine above-threshold co-owner rather than a coverage gap: DASH-STORY-018 (0.0575 margin, python-backend-engineer 0.8480 vs database-engineer 0.7905) and, more loosely, DASH-STORY-015 (0.1195) and DASH-STORY-017 (0.1080). All three are preference decisions, not coverage gaps, and are pre-scored for a rebalance without a new AR.0-equivalent scoring pass if needed (see AR0-S2-F2).
